post.description:
This endpoint is used for generating a Pix charge.

Pix creation is synchronous, but registration with the financial institution is performed in the background. Therefore, the request response will not contain the `qrcode` field.

To receive the qrcode, it is necessary to sign a webhook to receive the complete Pix payload when the registration is confirmed.

## Prerequisite

To issue a Pix charge, it is necessary to have a Pix Account registered in your account. Every Pix belongs to a Pix Account that represents the payment institution and the key that will be used to issue the Pix.
The Pix Account creation must be done through the system's web interface or through the endpoint `POST /api/v2/charge/pix_accounts`.

## Webhook Events

When registering a Pix, the system creates a command to register the PIX with the financial institution and the `pix.register.requested` event is triggered. After the Pix registration is confirmed at the institution, the `pix.register.confirmed` event is triggered.

The `pix.db.created` event is also triggered in this operation.

put.description:
> **Asynchronous Processing:** This endpoint is processed asynchronously and creates an update command for the PIX.
PIX update is done asynchronously, that is, when receiving the request, our API stores the changes you are requesting and creates a Command. This command is processed in the background and after confirmed, the Pix is updated. You receive in the response of this request the ID of the created command and can query it anytime. See more in [List Pix Commands](ref:get_v2-charge-pix-pix-id-commands) and [View a Command](ref:get_v2-charge-pix-pix-id-commands-id).

## Webhook Events

When the request is made, a `pix.update.requested` event is triggered.
Our server then begins attempts to send the change to the financial institution.
Only after it is confirmed at the financial institution, then the pix is updated.
At this moment the `pix.update.confirmed` event is triggered.

The `pix.db.updated` event is also triggered on confirmation of this operation.
> ⚠️ **Attention to return payload:** The response of a PIX update call is the payload of a Command. Inside the command payload there is the `pix` key with the PIX data in question.

put.description:
> **Asynchronous Processing:** This endpoint is processed asynchronously and creates a cancellation command for the PIX.
Cancellation of a PIX is done asynchronously, that is, when receiving the request, our API stores the request and creates a Command. This command is processed in the background and after confirmed, the Pix is cancelled. You receive in the response of this request the ID of the created command and can query it anytime. See more in [List Pix Commands](ref:get_v2-charge-pix-pix-id-commands) and [View a Command](ref:get_v2-charge-pix-pix-id-commands-id).

## Webhook Events

When the request is made, a `pix.command.cancel.started` event is triggered.
Our server then begins attempts to send the cancellation to the financial institution.
Only after it is confirmed at the financial institution, then the pix is cancelled in our database.
At this moment the `pix.command.cancel.confirmed` event is triggered.

The `pix.db.updated` event is also triggered on confirmation of this operation.
> ⚠️ **Attention to return payload:** The response of a PIX cancellation call is the payload of a Command. Inside the command payload there is the `pix` key with the PIX data in question.

post.description:
Requests the current balance of a financial account from the financial institution. Requires an active connection.
> **Asynchronous Processing:** This endpoint creates a balance synchronization command for the Financial Account.

Upon receiving the request, our API creates a Command, which is processed in the background. When the bank
responds with the balance, the command is confirmed and a new balance is recorded in the Financial Account. You receive
in the response to this request the created command and can query it at any time in
[List Commands of a Financial Account](ref:get_v2-financial-accounts-account-id-commands) and
[View a Command](ref:get_v2-financial-accounts-account-id-commands-id). The recorded balance appears in
[List balances](ref:get_v2-financial-accounts-financial-account-uid-balances).

To be able to run the Balance Synchronization, there must be an active Connection (that is, validated and
enabled) associated with the Financial Account, and its financial provider must offer balance queries
via API. Otherwise, the response is `422` with `param: financial_account`.

## Webhook Events

When the request is made, a `financial.account.balance_sync.requested` event is triggered.
After the response from the financial institution, the `financial.account.balance_sync.confirmed` event is triggered.

get.description:
Query the status of a requested statement synchronization.

The status is recalculated with each query from the request commands:

* `pending` - no command has started processing
* `processing` - in progress (part of commands have finished)
* `done` - all commands have been confirmed and transactions are already available in
  [List Transactions](ref:get_v2-financial-accounts-financial-account-uid-statement-transactions)
* `partial` - all finished, but part failed. The `commands` array shows which window failed and why
* `failed` - all finished and none were confirmed

The `commands` array brings each command with its own window in `params.start_at`/`params.end_at` and the
error message in `error_message`, when applicable. It is through it that **which month** failed in a
multi-month synchronization is identified.

get.description:
Lists the transactions of the statement of a financial account, filtering by period, type, amount, and description.

## Date window — scheduled change

Today, a request without dates returns the entire statement of the account. This behavior
**will change on 05/02/2027**: the query will always run within a window of at most
180 days, which is what keeps the endpoint fast on accounts with long history.

You can adopt the new behavior right now by sending `date_window=strict`, and you should do it
before the cutoff date. With it:

| Parameters sent | Window queried |
|---|---|
| none | The last 180 days |
| only `occurrence_date_from` | 180 days from it |
| only `occurrence_date_to` | 180 days before it |
| both | The informed period, as long as it does not exceed 180 days |

An interval greater than 180 days is rejected with `422` instead of being silently reduced — a partial statement that looks complete is worse than an error. For longer periods, make successive calls of up to 180 days each.

As long as `date_window=strict` is not sent, nothing changes. Requests whose result **would be
different** under the strict window respond with the headers `Deprecation: true` and
`Sunset: Fri, 05 Feb 2027 00:00:00 GMT` — use them to discover which of your integrations
need adjustment.

post.description:
Synchronizes the bank statement of a financial account. Fetches transactions directly from the financial institution through API. Requires active connection.
> **Asynchronous Processing:** This endpoint is processed asynchronously and creates a statement synchronization command for the Financial Account.

Statement synchronization of a Financial Account is done asynchronously, that is, when receiving the request, our
API stores the request parameters and creates a Command. This command is processed in the background and then confirmed
and the transactions will be imported into the Financial Account. You receive in the response of this request the ID of the created command
and can query it anytime.

See more in [List Financial Account Commands](ref:get_v2-financial-accounts-account-id-commands) and
[View a Command](ref:get_v2-financial-accounts-account-id-commands-id).

In order to execute the Statement Synchronization, there must be an active Connection (i.e., validated and enabled)
associated with the Financial Account.

## Synchronization Period

The fields `start_at` and `end_at` are optional and delimit the window to synchronize.
When omitted, the default window goes from **the first day of the current month until today**.

* informing only `start_at`, the end date assumed is today;
* informing only `end_at`, the start date assumed is the first day of the month of `end_at`;
* the end date cannot be in the future;
* the maximum period is **2 years** back from today.

Windows that span more than one calendar month are **sliced into one command per month**. This keeps each
request to the financial institution within a volume that the bank can respond to, and allows
reprocessing only the month that eventually fails. A window within the same month continues to create
a single command.

## Tracking the Import

In addition to the command in `data`, the response brings in `sync` the record of the requested import, with its own `uid`.
Use this `uid` to track the entire set — especially in multi-month windows, where
several commands are created — in
[Query Statement Synchronization](ref:get_v2-financial-accounts-financial-account-uid-statement-transactions-syncs-uid).

## Webhook Events

When the request is made, a `financial.account.statement_sync.requested` event is triggered.
Our server then begins communication with the financial institution's API to fetch transactions.
Only after it is confirmed at the financial institution, then the statement is updated.
At this moment the `financial.account.statement_sync.confirmed` event is triggered.

get.description:
Aggregates statement transactions into totals by group, instead of returning one line per transaction.

Answers questions like "how much did I spend on fees in July?" in a single request, with the
arithmetic done in the database — without paginating the entire statement.

> **The window here can reach 730 days**, against 180 from the listing. The response size is
> limited by the number of groups, not by history, so a long window is safe.

Accepts the same filters as the listing. If the combination of `group_by` and window generates more than
1000 groups, the request is rejected with `422` instead of returning a truncated summary — a total
cut in half looks complete and deceives silently.

The response also brings the `filters` and `meta` blocks, identical to those in the listing, with the addition
of `filters.group_by` informing the grouping applied.

get.description:
Catalog of categories that a statement transaction can carry.

Required to use the `category` filter in the listing and summary: the codes are a closed
domain, and without the catalog there is no way to discover that bank fees are code `105`.

The catalog has two natures: about 50 generic codes (`1xx` debits, `2xx` credits,
and `9999` for `others`) and hundreds of bank-specific codes, in the format
`1 + bank_number + bank_code` (e.g.: `107701`).

`kind` is derived from the slug and comes null when the category does not declare a side — which is the case
for most bank-specific codes. It is a convenience, not an exhaustive classification:
to sum inflows and outflows, use the `kind` filter from the listing or `group_by=kind`
from the summary, which operate on the actual type of the transaction.

post.description:
Registers a new connection with a financial provider.

> **Asynchronous Processing:** the `201` response is returned before the credentials are validated with the provider. The connection is created with `validated_at` and `validate_failed_at` null, and validation finishes in the background.

## Validation cycle

| State | `validated_at` | `validate_failed_at` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Validating | `null` | `null` |
| Validated | filled | `null` |
| Failed | `null` | filled |

When validation succeeds, `enabled_at` is also filled, even if the connection was created with `enabled: false`.

## Webhook Events

- `integration.connection.db.created`: fired by this operation, with the connection not yet validated.
- `integration.connection.db.updated`: fired when validation finishes, whether it succeeds or fails. Read the outcome in `object.validated_at` and `object.validate_failed_at`: the failure does not appear in `changes`.

put.description:
> **Asynchronous Processing:** This endpoint is processed asynchronously and creates an approval command for the Transfer Batch.
  The approval of a Transfer Batch is done asynchronously, that is, when receiving the request, our API stores the request and creates a Command. This command is processed in the background and after confirmed, the Batch has its status changed to Approved. You receive in the response of this request the ID of the created command and can query it at any time.

  ## Webhook Events

  When the request is made, a `transfer.transfer_batch.approve.requested` event is triggered.
  Our server then begins sending attempts to release the transfer to the financial institution.
  Only after confirmed at the financial institution, the batch is then marked as approved in our database.
  At this point the `transfer.transfer_batch.approve.confirmed` event is triggered.

  > ⚠️ **Attention to Approved status:** The Approved status is not terminal. When the financial institution confirms the transfers, they will have their status changed to Confirmed

> **Cancellation:** This endpoint cancels the Transfer Batch. The behavior depends on the registration state of the batch.

  - **Not registered with provider:** The batch is cancelled immediately in a local manner, without interaction with the financial institution. The response contains the updated batch.
  - **Registered with provider (cancellation API supported):** A cancellation command is created and processed asynchronously. The response contains the created Command.
  - **Registered with provider (cancellation API not supported):** A cancellation command is created per Transfer individually. The response contains the updated batch.

  Cancellation is possible in the states: `pending`, `awaiting_approval`, `confirmed` and `approved`.

  > ⚠️ **Attention to Cancelled status:** The Cancelled status is terminal.

post.description:
This endpoint is used to generate an Inter-Account transfer batch.

## Prerequisite

To issue a transfer batch it is necessary to have a Financial Account, specified in `financial_account_uid`. The transfer account applied to the batch is defined in `transfer_account_uid`; if omitted, the oldest one linked to the financial account is used; if provided, it must belong to `financial_account_uid`.

## Webhook Events

The `transfer.batch.db.created` event is triggered in this operation.

When registering a Transfer Batch, the system creates a command to register it with the financial institution. After the batch registration is confirmed at the institution, the `transfer.internal_batch.confirmed` event is triggered.

The `transfer.db.created` event is also triggered in this operation if the batch contains a new transfer.

put.description:
> **Asynchronous Processing:** This endpoint is processed asynchronously and creates a cancellation command for the Transfer.
The cancellation of a Transfer is done asynchronously, that is, when receiving the request, our API stores the request and creates a Command. This command is processed in the background and after confirmed, the Transfer has its status changed to Cancelled. You receive in the response of this request the ID of the created command and can query it at any time.

## Webhook Events

When the request is made, a `transfer.internal.cancel.requested` event is triggered.
Our server then begins attempts to send the cancellation to the financial institution.
Only after confirmed at the financial institution, the transfer is then marked as cancelled in our database.
At this point the `transfer.internal.cancel.confirmed` event is triggered.

> ⚠️ **Attention to Cancelled status:** The Cancelled status is terminal. The transfer can no longer be processed after cancellation.

post.description:
This endpoint is used to generate a pix transfer batch.

## Prerequisite

To issue a transfer batch it is necessary to have a Financial Account, specified in `financial_account_uid`. The transfer account applied to the batch is defined in `transfer_account_uid`; if omitted, the oldest one linked to the financial account is used; if provided, it must belong to `financial_account_uid`.

## Webhook Events

The `transfer.batch.db.created` event is triggered in this operation.

When registering a Transfer Batch, the system creates a command to register it with the financial institution. After the batch registration is confirmed at the institution, the `transfer.pix_batch.confirmed` event is triggered.

The `transfer.db.created` event is also triggered in this operation if the batch contains a new transfer.

put.description:
> **Asynchronous Processing:** This endpoint is processed asynchronously and creates an approval command for the Payment Batch.
  The approval of a Payment Batch is done asynchronously, that is, upon receiving the request, our API saves the request and creates a Command. This command is processed in the background and after confirmation, the Batch has its status changed to Approved. You receive in the response of this request the ID of the created command and can consult it at any time.

  ## Webhook Events

  When the request is made, a `payment.payment_batch.approve.requested` event is triggered.
  Our server then begins attempts to send the release to the financial institution.
  Only after confirmation from the financial institution is the batch marked as approved in our database.
  At this moment the `payment.payment_batch.approve.confirmed` event is triggered.

  > ⚠️ **Attention to Approved Status:** The Approved status is not terminal. When the financial institution confirms the payments, they will have their status changed to Confirmed

> **Asynchronous Processing:** This endpoint is processed asynchronously and creates a cancellation command for the Payment.
The cancellation of a Payment is done asynchronously, that is, upon receiving the request, our API saves the request and creates a Command. This command is processed in the background and after confirmation, the Payment has its status changed to Cancelled. You receive in the response of this request the ID of the created command and can consult it at any time.

## Webhook Events

When the request is made, a `payment.tax.cancel.requested` event is triggered.
Our server then begins attempts to send the cancellation to the financial institution.
Only after confirmation from the financial institution is the payment marked as cancelled in our database.
At this moment the `payment.tax.cancel.confirmed` event is triggered.

> ⚠️ **Attention to Cancelled Status:** The Cancelled status is terminal. The payment cannot be processed further after cancellation.

post.description:
Generic endpoint for creating payments of any type. The type must be specified in the `kind` field.

## Prerequisites

To issue a payment, you must have a Financial Account, informed in `financial_account_uid`. The payment account that records the operation is defined in `payment_account_uid`; if omitted, the oldest linked to the financial account is used; if informed, it must belong to `financial_account_uid`.

## Supported Types

### PIX
Use `kind: "pix"` and provide the `pix` key:
```json
{
  "kind": "pix",
  "financial_account_uid": "...",
  "amount": 100.0,
  "pix": {
    "qrcode": "00020126330014br.gov.bcb.pix..."
  }
}
```

### Bank Billet
Use `kind: "bank_billet"` and provide the `bank_billet` key:
```json
{
  "kind": "bank_billet",
  "financial_account_uid": "...",
  "amount": 200.0,
  "bank_billet": {
    "code": "81770000001-8 00005659970-7 41131079703-9 0014334-8"
  }
}
```

### DARF
Use `kind: "darf"` and provide the `darf` key:
```json
{
  "kind": "darf",
  "financial_account_uid": "...",
  "amount": 300.0,
  "darf": {
    "tax_code": "0107",
    "calculation_date": "2024-12-31",
    "expire_at": "2025-01-10"
  }
}
```

### Taxes
Use `kind: "tax"` and provide the `tax` key with bar code:
```json
{
  "kind": "tax",
  "financial_account_uid": "...",
  "amount": 400.0,
  "tax": {
    "kind": "iptu",
    "code": "81770000001-8 00005659970-7..."
  }
}
```

### Utility Bills
Use `kind: "utility"` and provide the `utility` key:
```json
{
  "kind": "utility",
  "financial_account_uid": "...",
  "amount": 500.0,
  "utility": {
    "code": "81770000001-8 00005659970-7..."
  }
}
```

## Webhook Events

The `payment.db.created` event is triggered in this operation.

> **Unified Endpoint:** This endpoint unifies the creation of all types of payments. To create payments of a specific type, you can also use the dedicated endpoints in `/api/v2/payment/{type}`.

post.description:
Creates a payment from just the barcode or the typable line. The payment type is resolved from the code itself, following the FEBRABAN v08 layout, and returned in the `kind` field of the response:

| Code | `kind` |
|---|---|
| 47 positions, or 44 not starting with `8` | `bank_billet` |
| starts with `8`, segment `2`, `3`, `4`, `6` or `7` | `utility` |
| starts with `8`, segment `1` or `5` | `tax`, with `tax.kind = "unknown"` and `tax.format = "code"` |

The code is rejected with `422` when a check digit does not match (the general one, in boleto and collection codes, and the field or block ones of the typable line), when it uses segment `9`, `0` or `8`, when the length does not match the first digit (47 positions starting with `8`, 48 not starting with `8`), or when it is an FGTS slip (segment `5` with agreement `0181` or `0182` in positions 16 to 19).

## Prerequisites

`payment_account_uid` is required and defines the source financial account. `financial_account_uid` is not accepted in this endpoint.

`amount` is optional when the code carries the amount to pay: collection codes with value identifier `6` or `8` (3rd position) and boletos with a non-zero amount. Without `amount`, the payment uses the code's amount; for a boleto, it is the face value, without interest, fine or discount. It is required for collection codes with identifier `7` or `9`, where the code's amount is only a reference, and when the code comes with a zero amount.

## Webhook Events

The `payment.db.created` event is triggered by this operation.

fine_type.description:
Type of fine:
                    * `0` No fine (`none`)
                    * `1` By amount (`amount`)
                    * `2` By percentage (`percentage`)
                    On return the data come in the `fine` object.

fine_amount.description: Fine amount in reals. Required when `fine_type` = `amount`.

interest_type.description:
Type of interest:
                    * `0` Does not apply / exempt (`none`)
                    * `1` Daily amount — calendar days (`daily_amount_calendar`)
                    * `2` Daily percentage — calendar days (`daily_percentage_calendar`)
                    * `3` Monthly percentage — calendar days (`monthly_percentage_calendar`)
                    * `4` Annual percentage — calendar days (`yearly_percentage_calendar`)
                    * `5` Daily amount — business days (`daily_amount_business`)
                    * `6` Daily percentage — business days (`daily_percentage_business`)
                    * `7` Monthly percentage — business days (`monthly_percentage_business`)
                    * `8` Annual percentage — business days (`yearly_percentage_business`)
                    On return the data come in the `interest` object.

                    * `5` Early payment by percentage — calendar days (`advance_percentage_calendar`)
                    * `6` Early payment by percentage — business days (`advance_percentage_business`)

beneficiary_cnpj_cpf.description:
CNPJ/CPF of Beneficiary.
                  When a valid CNPJ is sent, the data associated with the beneficiary of that CNPJ will be obtained automatically. Therefore, it is not necessary to include the following fields in the request:"
                    * `beneficiary_address_street` Beneficiary Street.
                    * `beneficiary_address_street_number` Beneficiary Street Number.
                    * `beneficiary_address_complement` Beneficiary Address Complement.
                    * `beneficiary_address_neighborhood` Beneficiary Neighborhood.
                    * `beneficiary_address_city` Beneficiary City.
                    * `beneficiary_address_state` Beneficiary State.
                    * `beneficiary_address_zipcode` Beneficiary ZIP Code.
                    * `beneficiary_address` Complete Address of Beneficiary.

name.description: Account name. Not received at creation or update, only returned in query and listing

status.description:
Wallet status:
When the wallet has just been registered, it receives the status `pending`.

At this point the user must accept the terms and start the homologation.

When clicking on "Proceed with Homologation", the status changes to `homologating`.

A boleto and a Homologation remittance will be generated to be sent to the bank. After completion, the status changes to `validating`.

From this point on, the user needs to inform the value of the boleto that was generated or send the return processed by the bank.

When the value is correctly informed, or in the processed return, the bank says everything is correct, the status changes to `active`.

* `pending` Homologation not started
* `homologating` In homologation, awaiting boleto payment
* `validating` Boleto paid, awaiting validation
* `active` Active and ready to use

default.description:
Default.
The `default` field determines the collection wallet that will be used in the creation of the boleto when no wallet is provided.

When the first wallet is homologated (moves to `status` = `active`), it receives the value `default` = `true`

customer_ignore_sms.description: Never send SMS to this customer

interest_type.description:
Interest/penalty type:
* `0` Non-existent (Default)
* `1` For daily percentage
* `2` For daily amount
* `7` For monthly percentage - Supported banks: Bradesco, BB, BTG, Caixa, Inter, Itaú, Safra, Santander, Sicoob and Sicredi

days_for_interest.description: Number of days after the due date when the penalty will start to accrue. The default value is 1 day (the day after the due date).

interest_percentage.description: Interest percentage. From 0.0 to 100.0 (Ex 1.5% = 1.5) Required if interest_type equals 1 or 7. Up to 2 decimal places.

interest_value.description: Daily interest amount (R$). Required if interest_type equals 2. Up to 2 decimal places.

interest_days_type.description:
Type of days for interest:
* `0` Calendar
* `1` Business

fine_type.description:
Fine type:
* `0` Non-existent (Default)
* `1` For percentage of boleto amount
* `2` For fixed amount

days_for_fine.description: Number of days after the due date when the fine will start to accrue. The default value is 1 day (the day after the due date).

fine_percentage.description: Late fee percentage Ex: 2% x R$ 250.00 = R$ 5.00. Required if fine_type equals 1. Up to 2 decimal places.

fine_value.description: Fine amount (R$). Required if fine_type equals 2. Up to 2 decimal places.

discount_type.description:
Discount type:
The discount type will be the same for all three discounts, if they exist. :
* `0` Non-existent (Default)
* `1` For fixed amount
* `2` For percentage of boleto amount

days_for_discount.description: Days for discount. Required if discount_type is different from 0 (zero)

discount_percentage.description: Percentage of the boleto amount equivalent to the discount. Required if discount_type equals 2

discount_value.description: Discount amount (R$). Required if discount_type equals 1.

second_discount_percentage.description: Percentage of the boleto amount equivalent to the second discount.

third_discount_percentage.description: Percentage of the boleto amount equivalent to the third discount.

charge_type.description:
Charge type:
* `1` Simple
* `2` Linked
* `3` Discounted
* `4` Vendor

dispatch_type.description:
Charge type:
When the boleto needs to be sent by mail. It is necessary to contract the service with the bank and you will pay a fee.
* `1` Customer
* `2` Bank

guarantor_city_name.description: City (Name must be correct and complete) of final beneficiary (Drawer/Guarantor)

divergent_payment_type.description:
Type of divergent payment:
Valid only for Itaú and Caixa.
* `1` Accepts any divergent amount
* `2` Accepts payments within a range of amounts or percentages
* `3` Does not accept divergent amount payments
* `4` Accepts payments above a minimum amount or percentage

divergent_payment_value_type.description:
Type of value to consider for payment limits:
Valid only for Itaú and Caixa.
* `1` Reports divergent payments by amounts
* `2` Reports divergent payments by percentages

divergent_payment_maximum_value.description: Maximum value for divergent payment range.

divergent_payment_minimum_value.description: Minimum value for divergent payment range.

divergent_payment_maximum_percentage.description: Maximum percentage for divergent payment range.

divergent_payment_minimum_percentage.description: Minimum percentage for divergent payment range.

divergent_payment_limit.description: Number of payments allowed. Required if divergent payment data is provided. Used only by Caixa.

prevent_registration.description:
Prevent sending registration to bank:

If `true`, prevents the boleto from being registered. To be used in cases where the boleto was already registered outside of Kobana but you want to include it in the system.

custom_attachment_name.description: Name to be used in boleto files sent to the customer in notifications. Accepts use of variables. If left empty, the default is the word "boleto" followed by the ID.

updated_at.description: Boleto last update date and time

payment_count.description: Number of partial payments accepted for this boleto.

* `offer` (Journey 4) User joined via composite QR Code with expiration (requires pix_uid and location)

With `validated_at` also null, it distinguishes "validation in progress" (this field null) from "failed and will not change on its own" (this field filled). It may remain filled even after a successful credential validation when `association_failures` is not empty: the two outcomes are independent.

credentials.description: Credentials.

enabled.description: Enable connection

revalidate.description: Revalidates credentials with the financial provider. If passed true, the connection will only be changed if the credentials and permissions are valid.

status.description: HTTP status code of the error. Ex: `400`.

title.description: Brief description of the error. Ex: `Invalid API Token`.

param.description: Name of the parameter that failed validation. Ex: `amount`.

detail.description: Detail of the validation that generated the error. Ex: `cannot be blank`.

data.description: The connection itself (created or updated, even when an association was rejected) or the uid of the conflicting connection (credentials already in use by another connection in the account).

conflicting_connection_uid.description: UID of the connection that already holds these credentials.

uid.description: Public identifier (UUID) of the Command. Used as a parameter in individual query (`GET /commands/{uid}`).

status.description:
Command status.

`pending`: Command not yet executed. [Initial State]
`confirmed`: Command executed and confirmed.
`failed`: Command execution failed.

operation.description:
Operation type.

`register`: Registration.
`cancel`: Cancellation.
`update`: Change.
`add`: Inclusion.
`remove`: Removal.
`approve`: Release.
`reprove`: Rejection.
`reschedule`: Rescheduling.
`add_pix`: Add Pix to boleto.
`protest`: Protest.
`unregister`: Unregistration.
`refund`: Refund.
`retry`: Retry.

resource_type.description: Type of resource to which the Command belongs (ex.: `BankBillet`, `Pix`, `Financial::Account`).

resource_uid.description: Public identifier (UUID) of the resource to which the Command belongs.

financial_provider_slug.description: Slug of the financial provider (bank) responsible for executing the Command.

payload.description: Server response with the result of the operation.

created_at.description: Date of creation of the Command record

updated_at.description: Date of update of the Command record.

confirmation_via.description:
Source of Command confirmation.

`api`: confirmed via response from the bank's API (includes webhooks, Recuperator and sync).
`edi`: confirmed via CNAB return (debit file).
`null`: No recorded source.

status.description:
Status.
`pending`: Pending. [Initial State]
`awaiting_approval`: Awaiting approval.
`confirmed`: Confirmed.
`reproved`: Disapproved.
`approved`: Approved.
`rejected`: Rejected.

Registration Status.
`pending`: Pending. [Initial State]
`requested`: Awaiting approval.
`confirmed`: Confirmed.
`rejected`: Rejected.
`failed`: Failed.

transfer_purpose.description:
Transfer Objective.
`01`: Collection
`03`: Electronic Payment boleto
`04`: Bank Reconciliation
`05`: Debits
`06`: Check Custody
`07`: Cash Management
`08`: Margin Consultation/Information
`09`: Consignment Averbation/Retention
`10`: Dividend Payment
`11`: Consignment Maintenance
`12`: Consignment of Installments
`13`: Consignment Abatement (INSS)
`14`: Consultation of Taxes to pay
`20`: Supplier Payment
`22`: Payment of Accounts, Taxes and Levies
`23`: Interoperability between Payment Institution Accounts
`25`: Buyer
`26`: Rotating Buyer
`29`: Payer's Allegation
`30`: Salary Payment
`32`: Payment of fees
`33`: Grant payment
`34`: Prebend payment (remuneration for priests and clergy)
`40`: Vendor
`41`: Term Vendor
`50`: Payment of Insured Claims
`60`: Payment of Traveler Expenses in Transit
`70`: Authorized Payment
`75`: Accredited Payment
`77`: Remuneration Payment
`80`: Payment of Representatives / Authorized Sellers
`90`: Benefit Payment
`98`: Miscellaneous Payments

financial_account_uid.description: UID of the Origin Financial Account

transfer_account_uid.description: UID of the origin transfer account. If the transfer account was not informed, the first transfer account that was associated with the financial account was used automatically.

confirmed_at.description: Date on which Kobana processed the operation confirmation. It does not necessarily represent the date the amount left the account — for that use transaction_date.

rejected_error.description: Rejection reason returned by the bank

transaction_date.description: Official settlement/debit date informed by the bank (authentication date). Reflects when the amount actually left the account.

transfer_kind.description:
Transfer type

`pix`: Pix.
`ted`: TED.
`internal`: Between Accounts

pix.description: Pix data (Present if the `transfer_kind` field is `pix`)

pix_type.description:
Pix type

`key`: Key.
`bank_account`: Bank account data

key_type.description:
Key type (Present if the `pix_type` field is `key`)

`cpf`: CPF.
`cnpj`: CNPJ.
`random`: Random.
`email`: Email.
`phone`: Mobile phone

key.description: Pix Key (Present if the `pix_type` field is `key`)

bank_account.description: Bank account data (Present if the `transfer_kind` field is `ted`)

compe_number.description:
COMPE code of the bank.

Examples: `1` (Banco do Brasil), `237` (Bradesco), `341` (Itaú)

ispb_number.description:
ISPB code of the bank.

If not provided in the input, it will be automatically inferred from COMPE when possible.

Examples: `0` (Banco do Brasil), `60746948` (Bradesco), `60701190` (Itaú)

judicial_deposit_number.description: Judicial deposit number (judicial deposit TED, Banco do Brasil only — mutually exclusive with `bank_account`)

judicial_deposit_bank_code.description: COMPE code of the judicial deposit's destination bank (`001` when the deposit is at Banco do Brasil itself). Present whenever `judicial_deposit_number` is filled

identifier.description:
Payment identification on the receipt from the financial provider. (Bank exclusive use)

Banks that accept this field (via API): Itaú

external_id.description: ID in your system. Optional for internal control.

custom_data.description: Hash with key and value in JSON format.

updated_at.description: Update date. ISO8601 format

v2_generic_transfer.description: Generic Transfer - Can be of any type (Pix, TED or Internal)

v2_new_generic_transfer.description:
New Generic Transfer.

The transfer type is specified by the 'kind' field:
- `kind: "pix"`: Creates a Pix transfer (data in `pix: {}`)
- `kind: "ted"`: Creates a TED transfer (data in `ted: {}`)
- `kind: "internal"`: Creates a transfer between accounts (data in `internal: {}`)

The 'kind' field is required and must be at the root level of the payload.

uid.description: Unique identifier of the DDA account (UUID). Use to consult, update, enable or disable via API.

cnpj.description: CNPJ or CPF of the company/person for which the DDA was enabled. Each Kobana account can have only one active DDA account.

name.description: Descriptive name of the DDA letter, automatically generated based on the company's data.

signers.description: List of signatories of the DDA adhesion letter (minimum 1, no maximum; two signatories cannot repeat `document_number` or `email`). Each signatory receives an email with a link for digital signature.

name.description: Full name of the signatory as per identity document.

email.description: Signatory's email for sending the digital signature link.

role.description: Signatory's position/function in the company. Values: `partner` (partner), `witness` (witness), `legal` (legal), `attorney` (attorney), `financial` (financial), `director` (director), `representative` (representative).

editable.description: Indicates if the account allows editing of signatories. `true`: newly created or re-enabled account — it is possible to add/remove/edit signatories. `false`: letter has already been generated and sent for signature — it is not possible to edit. To edit when `false`: disable the account (PUT /disable), enable again (PUT /enable), then update the signatories (PUT /dda_accounts/:uid).

status.description: Overall approval status of the DDA account. `pending` (awaiting completion of the adoption letter — signatories have not yet signed), `awaiting_approval` (letter signed by all — awaiting approval by Kobana Manager), `approved` (account approved and active — DDA boletos synchronized automatically — `enabled_at` field filled), `signature_rejected` (letter rejected by Kobana Manager — check `rejection_reason` and `rejected_at`).

letter_status.description: Status of the adoption letter PDF generation. `not_created` (PDF not yet generated), `creating` (generation in progress), `created` (PDF successfully generated — letter sent for signature), `failed` (generation failure — check `error_message`).

external_letter_status.description: Status of the digital signature of the adoption letter with the provider. `pending` (letter generated, awaiting sending for signature), `waiting_signatures` (letter sent — awaiting signatory signatures), `signed` (all signatories signed — letter completed), `failed` (failure in the signature process with the provider).

letter_signed_url.description: URL to download the signed DDA letter. When `external_letter_status` is `signed`, this URL points to the PDF signed by all signatories. The URL is managed via ActiveStorage and remains valid. Returns `null` when the letter has not yet been signed or is not available.

error_message.description: Detailed error message when a failure occurs in the adoption letter generation. Returns `null` when there is no error.

enabled_at.description: Date and time (ISO 8601) when the DDA account was enabled/activated, **confirmed by the provider**. When `null`, the account is disabled (or an enabling was requested and still awaiting confirmation — see `enable_requested_at`).

disabled_at.description: Date and time (ISO 8601) when the DDA account was disabled, **confirmed by the provider**. After disabling, there is a grace period of 21 minutes before being able to re-enable (provider requirement).

enable_requested_at.description: Date and time (ISO 8601) when the enabling was requested (via PUT /enable), still awaiting provider confirmation. When present and `enabled_at` is still `null`, the account is in the "awaiting confirmation" state. Becomes `null` again once confirmation arrives.

disable_requested_at.description: Date and time (ISO 8601) when the disabling was requested (via PUT /disable), still awaiting provider confirmation. When present and `disabled_at` is still `null`, the account is in the "awaiting confirmation" state. Becomes `null` again once confirmation arrives.

validated_at.description: Date and time (ISO 8601) when the DDA letter was validated/approved by Kobana Manager.

rejected_at.description: Date and time (ISO 8601) when the letter was rejected by Kobana Manager. Filled when `status` is `signature_rejected`.

rejection_reason.description: Reason informed by Kobana Manager when rejecting the membership letter. Filled when `status` is `signature_rejected`.

bank_billets_sync_last_updated_at.description: Date and time (ISO 8601) of the last successful synchronization of DDA boletos. Indicates when the system fetched and processed new boletos from the provider for this account.

created_at.description: Date and time (ISO 8601) when the DDA account was created on the Kobana platform.

updated_at.description: Date and time (ISO 8601) of the last update of this DDA account.

business_legal_name.description: Legal name of the company associated with the CNPJ of the DDA account. Optional field, provided directly by the API client (without automatic CNPJ lookup).

phone_number.description: Contact phone of the company associated with the CNPJ of the DDA account. Optional field.

address.description: Address of the company associated with the CNPJ of the DDA account. All subfields are optional. Returns `{}` when no subfield was provided. An update replaces the entire hash — does not merge partially with the previous value.

zip_code.description: CEP (format 99999999 — dashes and other non-numeric characters are automatically removed).

state.description: State abbreviation. Must be a valid Brazilian state.

cnpj.description: CNPJ or CPF of the company/person for which the DDA will be enabled. Must be a valid document. Each Kobana account can have only one active DDA account.

signers.description: List of signatories of the DDA adhesion letter (minimum 1, no maximum; two signatories cannot repeat `document_number` or `email`). Each signatory will receive an email with a link for digital signature.

name.description: Full name of the signatory as per identity document.

document_number.description: CPF of the signatory (format: 000.000.000-00 or numbers only).

email.description: Email of the signatory to send the digital signature link.

role.description: Position/role of the signatory in the company. Optional field. Values: `partner` (partner), `witness` (witness), `legal` (legal), `attorney` (attorney), `financial` (financial), `director` (director), `representative` (representative).

uid.description: Unique identifier of the DDA boleto (UUID). Use this value to query, release, or reject the boleto via API.

status.description: Internal status of the DDA boleto on the Kobana platform. Represents the client approval flow: `pending` (available for action: release or reject), `released` (released by client for payment — field `released_at` filled), `rejected` (rejected by client — irreversible transition — field `rejected_at` filled), `paid` (paid via Kobana — field `payment_uid` filled).

external_status.description: External status of the boleto informed by the provider. Completely independent of the `status` field and can change at any time via synchronization. `open` (open, available for payment), `overdue` (overdue — interest and penalties may apply), `paid` (paid confirmed by bank — may occur before or independent of `status: paid`), `canceled` (canceled by beneficiary or bank), `downloaded` (downloaded — equivalent to paid for internal processing purposes), `blocked` (blocked — the boleto was created but is not yet available for payment).

barcode.description: Barcode of the boleto (44 digits). Can be null when the boleto is still in initial synchronization phase.

line.description: Typable line of the boleto — formatted representation of the barcode for manual entry. Can be null during initial synchronization.

our_number.description: Our number assigned by the issuing bank. Unique identifier of the boleto in the beneficiary's banking system.

description.description: Description or instructions of the boleto informed by the beneficiary (cedent).

nominal_amount.description: Original (face) value of the boleto in reais (BRL), without surcharges or discounts. May differ from `amount` after maturity when interest/penalties are applied.

amount.description: Updated value of the boleto in reais (BRL), already considering applicable interest, penalties, discounts, and allowances. May differ from `nominal_amount` after maturity.

min_payment_amount.description: Minimum amount accepted for boleto payment in reais (BRL). Relevant when `allow_parcial_payment` is `true`.

max_payment_amount.description: Maximum amount accepted for boleto payment in reais (BRL).

expire_at.description: Boleto maturity date (ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DD). After this date, interest and penalties may apply as configured by the beneficiary.

issue_date.description: Boleto issuance date by the beneficiary (ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DD).

reference_month.description: Reference/competency month of the boleto (e.g.: month of the charged service). Values in English.

beneficiary_name.description: Name or legal name of the beneficiary (cedent) — company or person who issued the boleto and will receive payment.

beneficiary_cnpj_cpf.description: CPF or CNPJ of the beneficiary (cedent).

beneficiary_bank_name.description: Name of the bank where the beneficiary has an account for receiving.

beneficiary_bank_number.description: COMPE code (3 digits) of the beneficiary's bank. Ex: `001` (Banco do Brasil), `341` (Itaú), `237` (Bradesco).

owner_cnpj_cpf.description: CPF or CNPJ of the payer (drawee). Corresponds to the CNPJ/CPF registered in the DDA account.

owner_person_name.description: Name or legal name of the payer (drawee) — company or person in whose name the boleto was issued.

fine_amount.description: Fixed amount of late penalty in reais (BRL). Applicable after `fine_date`.

fine_percentage.description: Percentage of late penalty on the boleto value. Applicable after `fine_date`.

fine_date.description: Date from which the late penalty starts to be charged (ISO 8601 format).

interest_amount.description: Fixed amount of interest per day late in reais (BRL). Applicable after `interest_date`.

interest_percentage.description: Percentage of interest per day/month late. Applicable after `interest_date`.

interest_date.description: Date from which late interest starts to accrue (ISO 8601 format).

discount_amount.description: Fixed discount amount for early payment in reais (BRL). Valid until `discount_date`.

discount_date.description: Deadline to obtain the early payment discount (ISO 8601 format). After this date, the discount does not apply.

reduction_amount.description: Value of the allowance granted by the beneficiary in reais (BRL). Different from discount, allowance reduces the total amount regardless of payment date.

allow_parcial_payment.description: Indicates whether the boleto accepts partial payment (value less than total). When `true`, payment can be made with a value between `min_payment_amount` and `max_payment_amount`.

released_at.description: Date and time (ISO 8601) when the boleto was released for payment by the client. Filled only when `status` is `released` or `paid`.

rejected_at.description: Date and time (ISO 8601) when the boleto was rejected by the client. Filled only when `status` is `rejected`.

payment_uid.description: UUID of the Kobana payment linked to this DDA boleto. Allows tracking the payment originated from this boleto. Filled when the boleto is associated with a payment via API.

dda_account_uid.description: UUID of the DDA account (Dda::Account) that originated this boleto. Allows assigning each boleto to its DDA account when the macro account has multiple DDA accounts (distinct CNPJs). Null for legacy records not yet backfilled.

created_at.description: Date and time (ISO 8601) when the DDA boleto was received and registered on the Kobana platform.

updated_at.description: Date and time (ISO 8601) of the last update of this boleto (status change, data synchronization, etc.).

financial_account_uid.description: UUID of associated financial account

service_point_number.description: Service point number. Send `null` to clear the value.

cooperative_cnpj.description: CNPJ of the Sicoob cooperative of the account holder. Send `null` to clear the value.

external_id.description: External identifier of the payment account

balance_validation_enabled_at.description: Date and time when balance validation was enabled

remittance_enabled_at.description: Date and time when EDI remittance was enabled

remittance_enabled.description: Enables or disables generation of EDI remittances for this account.

created_at.description: Date and time of record creation

updated_at.description: Date and time of last record update

external_id.description: External identifier of the payment account

remittance_enabled.description: Enables or disables generation of EDI remittances for this account.

cooperative_cnpj.description: CNPJ of the Sicoob cooperative of the account holder.

Optional. When not provided, the remittance is sent as `98` (Miscellaneous Payments).
Provide it only if the bank requires a specific batch type: Itaú, for example,
rejects remittances whose batch type the company has not contracted.

Payments with different purposes are sent in separate remittances, because the
service type describes the whole batch.

For payments, only Itaú currently reads this field in the remittance. At the other banks the batch
type is fixed: the field is accepted and returned in the response, but does not change the file
sent.

v2_new_barcode_payment.description:
New Payment by barcode.

The type is resolved from the code itself (FEBRABAN v08 layout):
- bank boleto (44 positions not starting with `8`, or a 47-digit line) → `bank_billet`
- collection code with segment `2`, `3`, `4`, `6` or `7` → `utility`
- collection code with segment `1` or `5` → `tax`, with `tax.kind = "unknown"` and `tax.format = "code"`

An FGTS slip (segment `5` with agreement `0181` or `0182` in positions 16 to 19) is rejected with `422`.

`financial_account_uid` is not accepted: the financial account is the one of `payment_account_uid`.

code.description: Barcode (44 positions) or typable line (47 or 48 positions). Spaces, periods, hyphens and slashes are discarded.

amount.description: Amount. Optional when the code carries the amount to pay (collection code with value identifier `6` or `8`, or boleto with a non-zero amount): without it, the code's amount applies, which for a boleto is the face value, without interest, fine or discount. Required for collection codes with identifier `7` or `9` and when the code comes with a zero amount. When sent, it always prevails over the code's amount: to pay an overdue boleto with charges, send the amount including them.

payment_account_uid.description: UID of the source Payment Account. Required: there is no automatic selection.

beneficiary.description: Beneficiary information. Required when the code is a boleto and the financial account is BB.

document_number.description: Beneficiary CPF/CNPJ. Required when `kind = bank_billet` and the financial account is BB.

identifier.description: Payment identification on the financial provider's receipt.

external_id.description: ID in your system. Optional for internal control.

custom_data.description: Hash with key and value in JSON format.

external_code.description: Code or ID in your management system.

document_type.description: Document Type. Valid values: CPF, CNPJ

city_name.description: City. Name must be correct and complete

full.example: Av. Rio Branco, 26, Sobreloja, Centro, Rio de Janeiro, RJ. CEP: 20090-001

google_maps.example: Av. Rio Branco, 26, Centro, Rio de Janeiro, RJ

code.description:
Event code.

**IMPORTANT:** In addition to the events listed below, the system generates specific events by operation type:

- For **payments**, use: `payment.{tipo}.{operation}.{status}`
  - Types: `pix`, `bank_billet`, `darf`, `tax`, `utility`, `gru`
  - Operations: `register`, `approve`, `reschedule`, `cancel`, `get`, `sync`
  - Status: `requested`, `confirmed`, `failed`, `error`
  - Example: `payment.pix.cancel.confirmed`

- For **transfers**, use: `transfer.{tipo}.{operation}.{status}`
  - Types: `ted`, `pix`, `internal`
  - Operations: `register`, `reschedule`, `approve`, `cancel`, `get`, `sync`
  - Status: `requested`, `confirmed`, `failed`, `error`
  - Example: `transfer.ted.register.confirmed`

- For **batches**, use: `payment.{tipo}_batch.*` or `transfer.{tipo}_batch.*`
  - Example: `payment.pix_batch.register.confirmed`

status.description:
Query status:
* `pending` Pending (only when configured not to process automatically)
* `success` Successfully completed
* `error` Query failed

error_code.description:
Error code when `status` is `error`:
* `bank_billet_unavailable` Boleto unavailable: it may have already been paid, canceled or written off
* `document_not_supported` The provider did not confirm the document for payment: the agreement or modality may not be supported
* `provider_error` Provider failure while querying the boleto
* `unavailable_environment` Query available only in production

error_message.description: Error message when the query is processed but data is not returned.

pay_due_date.description: Payment deadline (grace period), when informed by the originating source

valid_for_payment.description: Indicates whether the boleto is eligible for payment at the time of the query

payment_status_reason.description: Reason returned when the boleto is not eligible for payment

allow_change_value.description: Indicates whether the payment amount can be changed within the returned limits

allow_partial_payment.description: Indicates whether the originating source allows partial payment

v2_account.description: Data of the token's account (organization). `id` and `uid` are always returned. The basic data (account_type, nickname, email, full_name, first_name, middle_name, last_name, business_name, parent_id, parent_uid, intercom_id — the latter is the same as the account uid) require the `organization.basic` or `login` scope. The other fields (gender, cpf, business_legal_name, business_cnpj, feature_flags, address, phone, billing, configuration, rate_limits, subscription) are only returned with the `all` scope, until the other `organization.*` scopes exist.

feature_flags.description: Feature flags enabled for the account

v2_oAuth2.description: OAuth2 with PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) support. Public clients (mobile apps, SPAs) must use PKCE. Confidential clients (with client_secret) may optionally use PKCE.
